#5562. Olivia Culpo Brings 5-Week-Old Son to His First 49ers Game—Inside the Guest Room She Turned Into His Nursery

Olivia Culpo brought her 5-week-old son, Roman, to his first San Francisco 49ers game to cheer on dad Christian McCaffrey—months after transforming her guest room into his nursery.

The model, 34, took to Instagram to share a glimpse at the family game day, which saw her, Roman, and her daughter, Colette, 1, stepping out to watch McCaffrey, 30, take on the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium.

One of the snaps showed off their game-day attire, which included a 49ers shirt with "Daddy" on the back.

Another image showed Roman in his stroller and was captioned, "Roman's first game."

The beauty mogul also shared a photo of her and her daughter, which she captioned, “I’m not a regular mom, I’m a cool mom.”

Culpo also shared a video of her taking their children to embrace their dad after the game, adding, “We’re back with one more little fan in the stands this season. A little more love coming along for the game this season."

The model revealed that she welcomed their second baby on Sept. 29.

Months before, she revealed that she had transformed their guest room into a nursery. She shared that she overhauled the room her sister Aurora Culpo's kids Remi, 7, and Soleil, 5, tend to use when they visit.

"New baby's room for now. I wanted to keep the twin beds because Remi and Solei sleep here when they come over," she wrote alongside an image of the nursery she shared on her social media page in June.

The room boasted a neutral aesthetic with an animal theme.

At the time, she explained, "We also don’t know the baby’s gender yet, so this feels perfect neutral for now. Honestly, newborns don’t really sleep in their room in the beginning anyway because they’re eating around the clock. That’s one of the reasons I’ve never felt the need to find out the gender to 'have the nursery ready.'"

That same month Culpo revealed she and her spouse were in the process of giving their $14.5 million property a head-to-toe overhaul to ensure it was looking its very best by the time the newest member of their family was born.

Culpo and McCaffrey purchased the Fryman Canyon, CA, dwelling from actor George Clooney in 2025, but they are now steadily eradicating all traces of the "Ocean's Eleven" star from the home in a bid to turn it into their dream family abode.

Revealing a sneak peek at the changes, Culpo pointed to one particular area of irritation that she has since transformed: dual bathrooms that sat next to each other with their own doors.

"Remember the two bathrooms next to each other that made no sense? All gone! I moved the door to the kitchen and now it will be a scullery,” Culpo wrote alongside an image of her hallway with the offending bathrooms on full display.

But the model did not stop there, moving on to several other spaces in the house, all of which have been given a stunning facelift, outfitted with new wallpaper, paint, and upgraded floors.

She then shared before-and-after images of the dining room, revealing that the space has been completely cleared of all previous decor, including the industrial lighting fixture that hung in the middle of the room, as well as the orange curtains and white wood-paneled ceilings.

The space has, instead, been given a fresh new aesthetic, complete with patterned wallpaper, hardwood flooring, exposed wooden beams, and an elegant crystal chandelier hanging at the center of the space.

“Currently … Dining table and chairs going in soon!," Culpo captioned the video of the newly revamped room.

The dwelling serves as the primary residence for the model and her husband, who is currently one of the leading players on the San Francisco 49ers.

The opulent six-bedroom, six-bathroom abode sprawls across 7,354 square feet, giving the couple plenty of room for their growing family.

Inside, the home boasts a library, screen room, and wine wall.

Culpo and McCaffrey purchased the home from Clooney, 65, who bought it from Fleetwood Mac singer Stevie Nicks for $2.2 million in 1995.

One month after splashing out a staggering sum on the property, Culpo gushed about it on Instagram.

"Now onto my next project, the most exciting one of all. Our forever home. So much original character to protect in this home, it’s going to be such a special project," she said.

The couple's purchase came four months after they tied the knot in a lavish Rhode Island ceremony attended by their close friends and family.

At the time, Culpo told People magazine, "I loved every part of my wedding. I love my husband and the people we got to celebrate that day with."

Three months before they said "I do," Culpo revealed she was ready to start expanding her family, joking that she was going to "rip out [her] IUD” and “start trying immediately” after the wedding.

The former Miss Universe also holds the keys to a $3.5 million property in Encino, CA, which she purchased in 2019 and which served as her and McCaffrey's main residence during the NFL offseason.

In 2021, she told Architectural Digest she purchased the five-bedroom, seven-bathroom property to get away from the "noise" of Hollywood.

“I realized I really wanted something that felt more calming, like a sanctuary almost. A respite from the city,” she said at the time.

McCaffrey previously owned a North Carolina mansion, which he sold in 2024 for $12.5 million, and a Charlotte, NC, condo, which he let go of in 2024 for $3 million.

In recent months, Culpo has confessed that the couple keep their romance alive during her spouse's busy season by "prioritizing date nights at least twice a month."

“During the season, it can be a little more difficult. Just prioritizing one-on-one time," she told E! News in September.

#5561. David Muir Shares Rare Look at Personal Life Ahead of His Birthday—Inside His $7 Million Lakeside Estate in Upstate New York

When it comes to his personal life, famed journalist David Muir tends to keep quiet, but the “World News Tonight” anchor recently pulled back the curtain just before his 53rd birthday.

In a Nov. 7 Instagram post, the ABC News anchor shared a wholesome update—a snap of his German short-haired pointer, Axel, as the pair set out to enjoy the fall foliage.

Although Muir let the photo speak for itself—offering nothing more than an autumnal leaf emoji as the caption—he occasionally uploads content of Axel, usually to show off their outdoor adventures.

In a 2025 interview with People magazine, the broadcaster shared some rare insight into his home life, noting that while he’s based in Manhattan for work, he enjoys retreating to a spot just outside his hometown of Syracuse.

“I’d say my most comfortable element is being outside, covered in mud,” he told the publication, adding that he had recently taken a trip to his property in upstate New York, enjoying the surroundings despite the fact that it had been “pouring rain.”

In 2019, Muir purchased a $7 million property on Skaneateles Lake—a small town about a 30-minute drive from Syracuse.

“This job takes me all over the world, and I can’t think of a better place to catch my breath,” he told Syracuse.com at the time.

The 4,300-square-foot abode is a single-family home set on a 6-acre plot of land with water access. The six-bedroom, 2.5-bathroom dwelling was built in 1890 and seems to be the perfect place to escape from the bustle of the city—or a job as demanding as Muir’s.

“When you’re out there on the lake, smelling the same air that you smelled when you were on your BMX bike back when you were a kid, there’s something really fueling about that and connected about it,” he told People magazine in 2025. “You just feel like you’re home again.”

Over the years, Muir has invited his Instagram followers to enjoy the dazzling lake views he enjoys during his weekends away.

In a 2020 post, he remarked, “I love being home,” in a caption of a photo of himself cracking a smile while enjoying a boat ride across the lake.

A few distinct features of Muir’s historic home have taken up real estate on his Instagram profile, as well, including the charming wraparound porch that hugs the Skaneateles Lake property, which made an appearance in a 2022 post he shared for his sister’s birthday, where he made a note to give a shoutout to “porches.”

He purchased the 2,280-square-foot abode for $4.2 million in 2013, the same year he became the host of “World News Tonight,” following in Diane Sawyer’s footsteps.

Located on West Fourth Street, the three-bedroom, three-bathroom structure was built in 1877 by Alexander M. McKean, and Muir put it on the market for $7.5 million in April 2025.

“Inside, the original details of this 15 foot wide house have been lovingly restored,” the listing explained. “The renovation maintains and respects the character of this remarkable home, while bringing it completely up-to-date, upgrading electricity, plumbing, and gas service but keeping and restoring original details including hardware, flooring, fixtures, and historic plaster medallions and moldings throughout.”

Perhaps the most stunning feature of the townhouse was the primary bedroom, which spanned the entire fourth level of the building. With a bed area that faced over quiet gardens and a full wall of closets, the suite also included a spacious office and a windowed bathroom with a vintage claw-foot tub.

The home lingered on the market for a few weeks before it was removed and relisted, but nearly six months later, it was sold for $6.85 million.
